### What the session covers

**Part 1 · The basics.** The Claude Code screen; picking a model and an effort
level; why a long conversation gets narrower, not dumber, and Git as the safety
net; `CLAUDE.md` as the place your defaults live; what a skill and a slash
command are; the Sandbox and the Allow / Ask / Deny permissions.

**Part 2 · The live demo.** A proposal in Word becomes a deck on our template.
One command, walked through step by step, including the review gate where you
confirm the slide plan before anything is built, and the iteration that follows
("add a timeline slide", "shorten the methodology to three bullets").
:::

::: {}
### How it works

The folder has one skill, `/proposal-to-slides`. It reads the brand defaults in
`CLAUDE.md` (template file, colours, fonts, bullets per slide), renders the
template to images to copy its look, proposes a slide plan and waits for your
go-ahead, then builds the `.pptx` and checks it page by page.

The pedagogical point is the gate. The skill is not allowed to produce a deck
you have not seen the outline of.
:::
:::

### Replicate it

::: {.steps}
1. Download the zip above and unzip it. Open a terminal in the `01_slidemaker` folder.
2. Make sure the tools the skill calls are installed: **Node.js** (the deck is built with `pptxgenjs`), **LibreOffice** and **Poppler** (to render and check the result) and **Pandoc** (to read `.docx` input). None of these need Python.
3. Start Claude Code and run the skill on the sample proposal:
   ```text
   claude
   /proposal-to-slides input/research-proposal.md
   ```
4. Confirm the slide plan when asked. The deck lands in `output/`.
5. Point it at one of yours: `/proposal-to-slides path/to/your-proposal.docx`.
:::

The same folder works in Codex: open it, and `AGENTS.md` tells the agent to
read `CLAUDE.md` and the skill, then do the same thing.
